title: 1933 United Airlines Boeing 247 mid-air explosion
summary: A Boeing 247 exploded and crashed near Chesterton, Indiana on October 10, 1933. The aircraft was carrying 3 crew and 4 passengers en route from Cleveland to Chicago when an explosive device detonated in the baggage compartment, fragmenting the structure and severing the tail section just aft of the toilet. The aircraft descended in flames and impacted a wooded area, with a secondary explosion occurring after impact. Investigators determined nitroglycerin was the probable explosive, though no suspect was identified.
probable_cause: On-board explosive device (bomb) in the baggage compartment.

factors.evidence: Explosive device detonated in baggage compartment; metal fragments riddled inside of toilet door and shards found wedged from impact.
Explosive device caused rapid explosive decompression through baggage compartment and fuselage breaching.
Tail section severed just aft of the toilet and found mostly intact nearly 1 mile away from main wreckage.
Second explosion followed after the aircraft crashed into the wooded area.

events.text: Explosive device detonated in baggage compartment shortly after 9 pm
Aircraft in flames at altitude around 1000 feet with tail section separating
Aircraft impacted wooded Jackson Township farm 5 miles outside Chesterton
Second explosion followed after aircraft crashed
